units.source_text: 不管在谁的眼里，对手是重病者，无论如何也难以同他对垒吧。

en.t: In anyone's eyes, his opponent was gravely ill, so it must have been hard, no matter what, to play against him.

units.source_text: 一方面是不愿让人家认为自己是趁对手生病，取巧获胜；

en.t: On the one hand, he did not want people to think he had taken advantage of his opponent's illness and won by opportunism;

units.source_text: 另一方面，倘使败北，更是声名狼藉。

en.t: on the other hand, if he were defeated, his reputation would suffer even more disgrace.
For the moment, victory and defeat had not yet been decided.

units.source_text: 名人一面对棋盘，自己便容易忘记病痛。

en.t: Once the Meijin faced the board, he himself could easily forget his illness and pain.

units.source_text: 这反而对想尽量把对手的病痛忘却的大竹七段不利。

en.t: This, if anything, worked against Otake 7-dan, who was trying as much as possible to forget his opponent's suffering.

units.source_text: 名人完全成了悲剧的人物。

en.t: The Meijin had become a completely tragic figure.
The newspapers also wrote as follows:

units.source_text: 名人谈过，纵令继续下棋，死在棋盘旁，也是出于棋手的本愿。

en.t: The Meijin had said that even if he continued playing and died beside the board, that too would be a player's true wish.

units.source_text: 他最后成了以身殉艺的名人。

en.t: In the end, he became a Meijin who sacrificed his body for his art.

units.source_text: 神经质的七段对对手的病痛漠不关心，也不同情，非要对弈不可。

en.t: The nervous 7-dan was indifferent to his opponent's illness and pain, felt no sympathy, and insisted that the match had to be played.
